 Taylor Swift loses it at CMA hosts’ joke about her wedding to Travis Kelce
 The singer and the NFL player wed at Madison Square Garden in July
 Anna Loren Friday 20 November 2026 00:10 EST

 Taylor Swift laughed out loud at a joke about her star-studded wedding to Travis Kelce during the CMA Awards ceremony.
 Swift, 36, returned to the Nashville awards on 18 November after a 10-year absence.
 She was nominated for single of the year for her Toy Story 5 song “I Knew It, I Knew You”, but ultimately lost out to Ella Langley , who took home the trophy for her mega-hit “Choosin’ Texas”.
 Introducing the awards, host Brad Paisley said: “We have to talk about the biggest story of the year. Somebody got married!”
 To cheers from the audience, he continued: “Blonde singer, football player... it was such a big deal.”
 Swift wed Kelce, who plays for the Kansas City Chiefs, in July at Madison Square Garden in New York City.
 However, Paisley’s co-host Lainey Wilson quickly interjected to reference her own wedding, telling Paisley “thank you for remembering” and showing him her ring.
 Wilson married former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Devlin 'Duck' Hodges in May at the Ruskin Cave in Tennessee.
 “What arena did you get married in?” Paisley asked Wilson.
 open image in gallery Taylor Swift at the 2026 CMAs ( Reuters ) “What arena are you talking about? I got married in a cave,” Wilson replied.
 She went on: “I will never forget what my husband said to me when we were looking for a wedding venue.”
 She and Paisley then sang the signature line from Lynn Anderson’s 1999 song “I Beg Your Pardon (I Never Promised You a Rose Garden)”, changing the lyrics to “I never promised you Madison Square Garden”.
 Swift was seen in the audience breaking into fits of laughter, leaning her head on her friend Brittany Mahomes’ shoulder, clapping, and saying “that’s good”.
 open image in gallery Taylor Swift and Keith Urban perform a mash-up of 'I Knew It, I Knew You' and 'Our Song' ( Reuters ) Paisley went on to say that he attended Swift’s wedding, saying: “Hi Taylor. Remember me? I ate all the shrimp.”
 Later in the ceremony, Swift was joined by country legend Keith Urban on the banjo as she performed a mash-up of “I Knew It, I Knew You” and “Our Song”, from her 2006 debut album Taylor Swift. 
 The awards also featured a tribute to the late Dolly Parton , who died of cancer in August.
 Langley took home six awards in total, including entertainer of the year, album of the year, and music video of the year.
